session_tail:
ther can honestly report absence. Each now sets the unknown flag. A failed file read did the same thing and now also sets it. I added a probe budget constant so an entry carrying more fingerprint patterns than the budget returns unknown up front rather than partially probing.

The one judgment call worth flagging: the probe cap short-circuits before any probing, rather than probing up to the budget and marking the remainder unknown. The test requires this, since its patterns would all match if examined.

**Why I aborted the anti-skill.** Two reasons, either sufficient.

- **The trap has no symptom.** The format is symptom-triggered, and the `symptoms:` field is the machine trigger built from literal observed error text. This bug throws nothing and logs nothing. It writes a wrong integer into a ledger and stays silent forever. The only signatures this session produced were a bare assertion failure and a missing-constant error naming one file, neither of which generalizes. Writing that field would mean inventing error strings nobody will ever see, which puts noise in the trigger index rather than a usable trigger.
- **No time was lost here to distill.** The failing tests stated the intended behavior outright, so the diagnosis took about two minutes. The mistake lives in a prior commit, not in this session's reasoning, and the procedure asks for a dead-end from the current session.

Underneath both, the lesson states as "a truncated search that found nothing means unknown, not absent," which a fresh Claude agrees with on sight. The real failure mode is attention drifting while adding a performance cap, and an injected skill does not catch that at the moment someone types a slice. The tests already in this repo do, permanently.

One near-duplicate supports the call. A prior session in this repo left a critique lock named for lossy transforms producing false negatives, which is the same trap family.

Nothing is committed. Say the word if you want the change on a branch.
